biography.plain_text: Goh Cheng Liang was a Singaporean industrialist who founded Wuthelam Group and built one of Asia's largest paint businesses. Beginning with surplus military paint after the Second World War, he developed his own Pigeon Brand and became Nippon Paint's Singapore distributor. Their partnership ultimately made his family the Japanese manufacturer's controlling shareholder.

long_biography.plain_text:
Raised in a crowded Singapore shophouse, Goh Cheng Liang left school early and worked selling fishing nets and in hardware shops. In 1949, he bought surplus British military paint, mixed colours by hand and sold the product under the Pigeon Brand. The venture grew into a paint shop and local manufacturing business.

Goh became Nippon Paint's main Singapore distributor in 1955 and formed a joint venture with the Japanese company seven years later. Their partnership expanded through Southeast Asia and into China, combining Nippon Paint's technology with Wuthelam's local sales and operating network. Goh also established a foundation that supported cancer care, including facilities and research programmes in Singapore.
long_biography.html:
Raised in a crowded Singapore shophouse, Goh Cheng Liang left school early and worked selling fishing nets and in hardware shops. In 1949, he bought surplus British military paint, mixed colours by hand and sold the product under the Pigeon Brand. The venture grew into a paint shop and local manufacturing business.

Goh became Nippon Paint's main Singapore distributor in 1955 and formed a joint venture with the Japanese company seven years later. Their partnership expanded through Southeast Asia and into China, combining Nippon Paint's technology with Wuthelam's local sales and operating network. Goh also established a foundation that supported cancer care, including facilities and research programmes in Singapore.
